Welcome

A Backyard Riding School That Grew Up.

It started in 2003 when neighborhood kids were drawn to four horses in a small stable. Today Rockin’ B has served over 1,200 students through year-round camps and lessons, in beginner-to-advanced English and western riding.


Read our history →
Why Rockin’ B

Built Around Safe, Confident Riders

Safety first

Camps cap at 4 riders per horse and 3 students per instructor, with a ground handler for every beginner.

Certified instructors

CHA-certified instruction, with staff trained and tested through our four-level program.

Indoor and outdoor arenas

Ride year-round, whatever the Alaska weather does, plus trails on adjacent parkland.

Real horse knowledge

Kids learn to groom, tack up, care for and ride, not just sit in the saddle.

Summer horse camps

Our 21st Year of Summer Camps

Weekly, Monday to Friday, for ages 5 to 16 and all skill levels. Campers help with ranch chores, learn horse care and anatomy, and ride daily in western, English and bareback tack, with scenic trail rides on adjacent parkland.

A Day at Camp

Morning: fill hay bags, feed horses, clean stalls and visit the farm critters.

Noon: lunch. Bring a healthy lunch, snacks and water, without sugar-loaded food or drinks.

Afternoon: groom, tack up and ride for up to an hour, then rotate through lessons, hands-on horse activities, crafts and lawn games.

Who we are

Owned by Rose and Bob English.

Rose is a retired Fort Worth barrel racer and former turn-back rider for a Texas cutting horse ranch. She taught lessons and guided trail rides in Tucson, and is a Certified Horsemanship Association instructor in English and western, with a focus on safety. Bob maintains the home, vehicles and property, and is her biggest support.


Meet Chevelle Beach, our onsite barn manager and CHA-certified instructor with 8 years of experience: (907) 341-7363.

Our history

Twenty Years of Weathering Storms.

Rose bought the property at 3741 Ptarmigan Terrace in 2001 and moved four horses up from Arizona in 2003. The indoor arena went up in 2008. We closed for a time after 2017, reopened as a boarding stable in 2019 and rebuilt the riding school, and came back strong after Covid. Many families stuck with us along the way.
